memory_candidates.content: When building fixture-based differential tests against an external formally-verified decision procedure (e.g. a Lean-built CLI binary), pin expected verdicts EMPIRICALLY by piping each hand-built fixture through the real binary first, rather than deriving expected output by hand-reasoning alone. Hand-reasoning about biconditional fixpoint clauses (e.g. an until/since local-coherence clause referencing neighbouring positions) is highly error-prone; the binary is cheap to invoke and is the actual contract. Record the binary's commit hash in the test module docstring so a later disagreement is diagnosable.

To construct a test fixture that proves a periodicity-collapse decision-procedure window bound is TIGHT (not merely sufficient), exploit the seam between a periodic region and the real (non-periodic) boundary it approximates: a position one period further back than the boundary has an identical LABEL to its periodic image, but its NEIGHBOUR (used by a fixpoint check referencing t+/-1) differs between the real boundary case and the periodic-reuse case. Building a violation that only manifests via that neighbour-mismatch, at a position outside the narrow window but inside the wide one, mechanically demonstrates the narrower bound is unsound. This generalizes beyond bimodal logic to any bi-infinite periodic-decoding verification scheme (lasso-shaped label/state sequences, ultimately-periodic traces, etc.).

When one task's report discovers a hard constraint (e.g. a wrong bound) that another, not-yet-started sibling task's plan currently gets wrong, amend that sibling plan directly and in-place (an explicit 'Amendment' block plus per-decision and per-phase inline annotations, sourced and dated) rather than filing a separate note to be applied later. Verify the amendment mechanically: re-run the target plan's own validator, and confirm invariant counts (phase heading count, status-marker count, a distinctive literal-pattern count) are unchanged from before the edit -- a plan-level check like 'grep -c "[NOT STARTED]"' will catch prose that incidentally reintroduces the literal bracketed status string outside a phase heading.
